headline: Auditable ML for peptide ADMET and binding prediction with realistic training data
label: Peptide Admet Prediction And Evaluation
summary: Recent preprints pair peptide ADMET prediction with simulated binding data, raising the bar for auditable model evaluation before candidate ranking.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning for peptide and macrocycle pharmacology, with ADMET prediction as the central endpoint. AIO targets cyclic peptides and macrocycles with an interpretable multimodal framework that uses solvent-aware contrastive pretraining. VReceptor generates sequence-dependent peptide binding data through a virtual receptor simulation that applies pharmacophore-inspired weighting, offering a route to training data for such models. Related work extends the interpretability concern to other modalities: PTM-BDL links typed post-translational modification states to drug response (IC50, resistance), with site-level integrated-gradients attributions, and ADCdb 2.0 compiles ADMET profiles for 542 antibody-drug conjugates alongside clinical and bioactivity data. What is new is the combination of simulated training data with attribution at the level of individual sites, which makes model behaviour inspectable before candidates are ranked.
